incident: Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again npm/PyPI supply-chain compromise

scope.scannerPackageSet: JFrog Here We Go Again package/version indicators plus selected confirmed broader Mini Shai-Hulud npm, PyPI, and Composer package/version indicators
scope.officialTanStackScope: 42 packages, 84 malicious versions, published on 2026-05-11 between 19:20 and 19:26 UTC
scope.campaignContext: JFrog reports more than 170 npm packages and 2 PyPI packages affected as of 2026-05-12. Socket reports 416 affected package artifacts for the broader Mini Shai-Hulud campaign as of 2026-05-12, spanning npm, PyPI, and one Composer artifact. Socket reports an active May 19 @antv npm publish wave tied to Mini Shai-Hulud and the npm maintainer account atool. Socket's technical analysis describes install-time index.js payloads, direct C2 at t.m-kosche.com, GitHub fallback exfiltration with reversed Shai-Hulud markers, and worm-like npm propagation through stolen npm tokens. May 22-23 ClickFix reporting and operator-provided VirusTotal context described compromised legitimate websites loading a remote script from staticcloudflare[.]pro with a reversed loader marker. Aikido's May 27 report describes codexui-android npm builds from 0.1.82 onward exfiltrating OpenAI Codex auth.json data to sentry.anyclaw[.]store/startlog. Aikido and OX's June 1 reporting describes 31+ compromised @redhat-cloud-services npm packages published via GitHub Actions OIDC/trusted publishing abuse, with a credential-stealing Mini Shai-Hulud variant calling itself Miasma, decoy api.anthropic.com traffic, and staged GitHub payload retrieval from letsgo0/sayyadina-phibian-159. Lupin & Holmes' May 14 node-ipc reporting describes malicious node-ipc 9.1.6, 9.2.3, and 12.0.1 publishes by the dormant atiertant maintainer identity, likely email takeover through the re-registered atlantis-software.net domain, DNS-tunneling exfiltration, and C2 at sh.azurestaticprovider.net. A June 3 operator-provided package table added exact @ccrm and @emcd-vue npm package/version indicators for the Moika follow-up cluster. Exact scanner detections are stored in this file; namespace and package-name warnings remain lower-confidence review prompts until exact malicious versions are confirmed.
